Not validated engineering or safety instructions. ML Mountain Rear Wheel. Fictional workshop demonstration for model 124, ML Mountain Rear Wheel, using representative product RW-M762. The draft covers hub preparation, wheel assembly, tire fitting, and simple checks.<Location LocationID="50" SetupHours="0.2" LaborHours="2.0" MachineHours="0.0" LotSize="1">Work Center 50 - Subassembly. Estimates are fictional demo assumptions. Subassembly: prepare the hub and assemble and check the representative wheel. This detailed routing is inferred from the historical work-center record.<step>Inspect 1 EA <material>HL Spindle/Axle (Product Number SD-9872)</material> and 1 EA <material>HL Shell (Product Number SH-9312)</material>; bring them together as the supplied hub components, without assuming unlisted internals. Check fit and movement before using the resulting <material>HL Hub (Product Number HU-8998)</material>.</step><step>Inspect 1 EA <material>ML Mountain Rim (Product Number RM-M692)</material>, 36 EA <material>Spokes (Product Number SK-9283)</material>, and 36 EA <material>LL Nipple (Product Number NI-4127)</material> for visible damage and verify the quantities.</step><step>Place the hub and rim in an assumed <tool>wheel-building stand</tool>. Connect the spokes between hub and rim with the nipples; illustration <diag>101241</diag> shows the component relationships, not a specified lacing pattern.</step><step>Using an assumed <tool>spoke wrench</tool>, adjust the nipples gradually. Spin the wheel in the stand and check for obvious wobble, loose connections, and interference.</step><step>Fit 1 EA <material>Mountain Tire Tube (Product Number TT-M928)</material> inside 1 EA <material>ML Mountain Tire (Product Number TI-M602)</material> and fit them to the rim, taking care not to pinch the tube. Follow the component manufacturer's directions for inflation.</step><step>Fit 2 EA <material>Reflector (Product Number RF-9198)</material> at compatible attachment points according to their supplied directions. Check that both are secure and clear adjacent parts.</step><step>Inspect the completed wheel for visible damage and seating irregularities; spin it and check for obvious rubbing or wobble. Set aside any assembly with an unresolved issue.</step></Location></root>
